page: Amazon Web Services c8g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the AWS Graviton4 platform. It features 96 dedicated physical cores based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, with one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity totals 192.0 GB, establishing a compute-focused 1:2 memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache configuration provides 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. The instance includes 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No dedicated hardware GPUs are present, and local storage is not bundled, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent or scratch disks.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward parallel scaling. In single-core benchmarks, including Geekbench and stress-ng single-thread tests, the processor registers within the middle 50th percentile. When leveraging all 96 cores, the instance reaches top-tier status across Geekbench multi-core (25,987.0), stress-ng multi-core (163,523.67), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (902.1 GB/sec). Memory subsystems show top-tier read bandwidth, sustaining 480.57 GB/sec on large uncached memory blocks and 11,078.9 GB/sec on cached blocks. Synthetic database tests and Redis SET operations also place within the top 10 percent, recording 193.42 million operations per second alongside 99.4 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The 96 dedicated ARMv9 cores deliver significant parallel throughput per unit of operational cost compared to smaller multi-threaded configurations, though applications must be compatible with arm64 instruction sets. Workloads dependent on local low-latency NVMe drives face tradeoffs due to the complete reliance on network-attached storage. The hardware profile aligns directly with heavily parallel compute tasks, distributed continuous integration and software compilation pipelines, batch processing engines, high-throughput static web frontends, and medium-footprint in-memory key-value caches.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores at 2.8 GHz and 192.0 GB of memory on the AWS Nitro System. Featuring a 1:2 memory-to-core ratio, it does not include local storage or hardware GPUs, depending instead on network storage and a 40 Gbps baseline network interface. While single-thread benchmarks place in the average tier, full-core utilization demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing, reflected in high Geekbench multi-core scores, fast Clang compilation, and extensive uncached memory bandwidth. Its compute density yields strong operational value for parallel processing, making it appropriate for large-scale software builds, batch data processing, distributed container workloads, and high-throughput web caching.
